headline: GOLD HITS 13-MONTH LOW AT $3,693.50 — RSI Approaches 31 as Short Covering Pushes Partial Recovery to $3,740
snippet: Gold fell to a fresh 13-month low of $3,693.50 on November 19 before staging a partial recovery to around $3,740 — driven by short covering rather than fundamentals, according to StoneX's Matt Simpson. The 14-period RSI is approaching 31, signaling developing oversold conditions, though Societe Generale said signals of a meaningful rebound are 'not yet visible,' with the December FOMC rate hike priced at approximately 90% probability continuing to suppress non-yielding assets.

headline: FIRST CANADIAN GRAPHITE DRILLS 43.9% CARBON AT ZONE 13 — Coarse-Flake Battery Anode Target Confirmed at Lac Guéret South, Québec
snippet: First Canadian Graphite (TSX-V: FCI) reported a 43.9% graphitic carbon sample with encouraging coarse-flake characteristics at Zone 13 of its Lac Guéret South project in Québec — the district-scale target that a September 2026 Phase II airborne survey indicated could be part of a much larger graphite system than previously understood. For battery supply chain investors, coarse-flake graphite for anode applications is a structurally undersupplied niche that remains strategically significant even as broad battery-metals sentiment is under pressure.

headline: NEM DROPS 5.7%, FCX 7.6% AS GOLD CRACKS $3,800 — Not One Analyst Holds a Sell Rating on Either Major Miner
snippet: Newmont (NEM) fell 5.7% and Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) dropped 7.6% on November 18 as front-month gold futures slid 2.7% below $3,800 on a surging dollar and rising Fed hike expectations — yet Schaeffer's reports that not a single analyst holds a Sell rating on either stock, a consensus gap that historically precedes capitulation and durable recovery in major mining equities rather than arriving after it.

headline: BAYRIDGE RESOURCES LOCKS UP REMAINING 49% OF BAKER LAKE URANIUM — Nunavut Project Consolidated to 100% via Binding LOI
snippet: Bayridge Resources (CSE: BYRG) signed a binding letter of intent to acquire the remaining 49% interest in its Baker Lake uranium project in Nunavut, Canada, bringing the company to 100% ownership of an Athabasca Basin-adjacent uranium asset at a time when uranium spot prices hold near $90/lb while uranium equities trade at multi-year lows relative to the physical market. Full ownership removes partnership complexity and positions Bayridge to advance the project independently into the next exploration phase.

headline: WAYFINDER METALS EARNS INTO 85% OF TWO DESEADO MASSIF GOLD-SILVER PROJECTS — CSE Junior Enters Argentina's Premier Silver District
snippet: Wayfinder Metals (CSE: WMC) signed a letter of intent to earn up to 85% interest in two gold-silver projects in Argentina's Deseado Massif — a Jurassic volcanic belt that hosts major operations including Cerro Negro, Manantial Espejo, and San José, and continues to attract early-stage capital despite Argentina's historically challenging regulatory environment. Junior earn-in structures in the Deseado Massif during precious metals bear markets have historically delivered strong returns for companies with the capital to advance projects through the cycle.

headline: NICKEL CREEK PLATINUM HALTS WELLGREEN DRILL AFTER 2 HOLES — 'No Significant Results'; Yukon Ni-PGM Program Needs New Financing
snippet: Nickel Creek Platinum (TSX-V: NCP) suspended its 2026 drill program at the Wellgreen nickel-platinum group metals project in Yukon after two holes failed to reach their approximately 600-metre target depths and returned no significant results — a reminder that even large advanced-stage nickel-PGM systems in Tier 1 jurisdictions face a capital wall in the current market. The company said resumption depends on securing additional financing, with no timeline provided.

headline: ZACKS: 4 GOLD MINING STOCKS LIKELY TO TIDE 2026 HEADWINDS — NEM, FURY, GROY, BTG Named as Best-Positioned for Recovery
snippet: Zacks Research names Newmont (NEM), Fury Gold (FURY), Gold Royalties (GROY) and B2Gold (BTG) as the four gold mining stocks most capable of weathering 2026's macro headwinds, citing NEM's P/E of 12.92x — below its 5-year median of 15.83x — alongside the structural advantages of royalty streamers and low-cost producers relative to development-stage peers during rate-tightening cycles. The analysis provides a framework for investors deciding whether to hold sector exposure through the December FOMC decision or exit before potential further downside.

headline: CRUX INVESTOR: INVESTORS RETURN TO GOLD AFTER HISTORIC SELLOFF — Market May Have Priced In More Downside Than the Fundamentals Justify
snippet: Crux Investor's November 19 analysis argues that gold's recovery from its 30%-plus decline since the US-Iran war premium began unwinding is being driven by genuine bargain-hunters returning to bullion positions rather than purely technical short-covering, and that the market may have overpriced December Fed hike risk relative to the structural demand floor provided by central bank purchasing running near 60 tonnes per month. The piece examines whether the $3,693 intraday low marks a durable inflection point or simply an oversold bounce ahead of the December 9 FOMC decision.

headline: USA RARE EARTH DIRECTOR BUYS $3M IN STOCK — Insider Bet Near Post-Earnings Lows as APEC Signals Bring Sector Relief
snippet: USA Rare Earth director Michael Blitzer disclosed a $3 million open-market purchase of USAR shares, lifting the stock after a period of significant selling pressure following the company's Q3 earnings miss and broader rare earth sector weakness — the stock had fallen approximately 37% in the month prior to the buy. Director-level purchases of this scale at or near sector lows have historically been a reliable forward indicator of management's internal confidence in project fundamentals, particularly for rare earth companies with long development timelines.

headline: COPPER PRICE DROP IGNORES ORE SHORTAGE AS CHINA SMELTING NEARS CAPACITY — Asia Copper Week: Most Extreme Financial-Physical Divergence Since 2015
snippet: Despite LME copper falling to seven-month lows near $12,770 per tonne, Crux Investor reports that delegates at Asia Copper Week described China's physical copper import premium as remaining near record levels — a disconnect that physical traders described as the most extreme divergence between financial and real copper markets since 2015. The analysis argues that speculative selling driven by AI-demand fears and dollar strength is masking a genuine ore shortage that Chinese smelters are working through near their processing capacity ceiling.
